The Watcher is the BOSS in the Blood Room of The Catacombs. In the Entrance floor, defeating them completes the run, but in all other floors, defeating them opens a portal to the main BOSS of that floor.

The Fight

[edit | edit source]

Overview

[edit | edit source]

When the Blood Room is first opened, The Watcher will say some dialogue, and then start spawning various Mobs. The amount spawned increases with higher floors, starting at 9 in Entrance and increasing by 1 with each floor.[1] These include multiple Undeads, as well as various MINIBOSS mobs in higher floors. These mobs first appear as heads in display cases on the walls, which the Watcher flies to when picking to spawn.

The Watcher cannot be damaged, and trying to do so will cause him to attack back with a laser. In Floor IV and above, he also has Watchful Eyes to prevent players from going more than several blocks up in the arena.

Players who are dead when the fight starts or die during the fight are reanimated as a hostile Wandering Soul that resembles the player who died. Killing a Wandering Soul will revive the player it resembles.

Once all of Mobs are summoned and killed, in the Entrance floor, the run completes. In all other floors, a portal will open to the main BOSS of that floor, and 1-2  Blessings of Time V and a  Blessing of Power V will spawn. There is also a 1.23% (1 in 81.3 rolls) chance for an  Optical Lens to drop.

Arena

[edit | edit source]
  • The Catacombs - Floor I.
  • The Catacombs - Entrance.

The Watcher's arena is fairly simple. There are 4 chains in the room with the Undead's and Player's heads on the wall. There are some corridors behind the Undead wall. A way to cheese the boss up to Floor III is to go on top of the portal, entrance door, or go on the second layer of the Undead. Keep in mind the top of the exit portal changes on every floor to represent the boss of that floor.

Higher Floors have changes to the Watcher's behavior:

  • Starting from Floor II, the Undead gain special perks according to their type.
  • Starting from Floor III, Bonzo can appear reanimated at the start of the fight. The reanimated Bonzo can perform his fireworks ability when brought down below 50%  Health.
  • Starting from Floor IV, the Watcher will be next to 2 Watchful Eyes, which deals 25% of the player's  Health as ✷ True Damage every second the player is too high up in the arena. Additionally, Scarf can appear at the start instead of Bonzo.
  • Starting from Floor V, all mobs spawned gain a random modifier. In just this floor, the modifier will be announced as dialogue before the fight begins. The Spirit Bear also can now spawn instead of Bonzo or Scarf.
Modifier Description
Healthy Grants 1.3x  Health, a 5% (1 in 20 kills) chance to drop a  Healing Tissue, and a 0.4% (1 in 250) chance to drop a  Vitamin Death.
Stormy Grants a 1% (1 in 100 kills) chance to drop Thunderlord VI on death. Every 5 seconds, there is also a 33.3% (1 in 3) chance to strike lightning to all players in a 6 block radius. This deals 2,000 /2,500 /5,000  in F5-F7 respectively, and 45,000 /60,000 /70,000  in M5-M7 respectively.
Golden Grants full  Golden Armor and drop  1 Gold Essence on death.
Speedy Grants increased  Speed and drops  Dungeon Potions of the equivalent floor tier.
Stealthy Makes the mobs invisible, except for their name tags and armor.
Boomer Makes the mobs wear  TNT on their head, which is triggered when they die. After a few second it explodes in a 5x5 radius, dealing 100% of the player's  Health as ✷ True Damage. This can be mitigated with  Absorption and the  Wither Cloak Sword. This also drops  Superboom TNT.
  • Starting from Floor VI, The Watcher no longer announces the modifier of its summons before starting. Additionally, Livid can appear instead of Bonzo, Scarf, or a Spirit Bear, dropping a  Livid Fragment. Additionally, Bonzo or Scarf can now drop their own respective fragment items.
  • In Floor VII, before any other spawns, one of Sadan's giants ( Bigfoot, Jolly Pink Giant, L.A.S.R., The Diamond Giant) will be reanimated. The pillars will be removed in the arena, making space for the Giant, although there's a rare chance the pillars won't be removed. Each one has a chance to drop its respective Precursor Relic, which can upgrade Wither Armor dropped from Necron.

Summoned Mobs

[edit | edit source]

The Watcher will spawn multiple Undead mobs with various names and appearances. These include Mr. Dead, Revoker, Tear, Skull, Walker, Cannibal, Frost, Putrid, Reaper, Vader, Flamer, Freak, Leech, Mute, Ooze, Parasite, and Psycho. They can also appear as Wandering Souls.

Additionally, starting from The Catacombs - Floor III, different reincarnations of previous BOSS mobs will start spawning. In The Catacombs - Floor VII, a random giant from the Sadan fight will also spawn.

Lore

[edit | edit source]
  • Before becoming The Watcher, he was a human known as Lathrop, he was a pupil and adopted son of Dr. Emmett after his parents died during the Calamity. Ever since The Breach on top of the mountain has opened, Lathrop started getting visions of a floating eye.
  • One day he is asked by Dr. Emmett to deliver a letter to his colleague in  Wilderness. He heads out and for some reason feels sad looking at the house he lived in. Entering the Inn, he was getting the feeling of Deja Vu. In the Inn he saw a man with black hair in black clothing. He recognized this from one of his visions. The mysterious man then leaves upstairs, a different man, a young assassin named Livid, comes to Lathrop and questions him about the mysterious man, since he claims to have never seen in the Inn before. Lathrop answers Livid's question saying that the mysterious man is a merchant from far away land, not knowing what lead him to say that since he in fact didn't know him. Livid then leaves back to his table and Lathrop too goes upstairs.
  • A while after, the mysterious man then left the Inn carrying Livid with him. Lathrop decides to follow him, as his feeling of Deja Vu grows stronger, despite him not remembering this. Necron figures out he is being followed and before the wooden entrance to The Catacombs he asks his pursuer, why is he following him. Lathrop explains his situation with visions and Deja Vu, then explains that he saw that by following Necron to his master, he will reach his full potential, as the door opened on their own, Necron urged Lathrop to follow him.
  • In Catacombs he meets The Wither King who leads him to his laboratory, in front of the Seeing-Stone, which immediately triggers a vision in him, he sees a house with a woman and a child inside, he recognizes the source of the command, Kaeman. The Wither King was impressed by Lathrop's natural abilities and in the following months, he made him use the Seeing-Stone again and again. Which transformed him to the limbless, one-eyed creature he now is.
  • Some time after, he was tasked to see Kaeman's past and use the orb to create a world, identical to the one Kaeman once knew, in which he could once again be happy. He has succeeded. Kaeman thanked the Watcher, which was a rare display from him and told him to be loyal to his new master - Necron, while he decided to stay in an enclosed chamber, dreaming of a happier time.
  • After the seclusion of their master, Necron decided to gather an army of necromancers for his goal and Watcher at some point wrote most of the Dungeon Journals. In 1531 AE, he watches the expedition to the Catacombs. He notices one particular member and his potential in necromancy, after learning his name, The Watcher decided to recruit Sadan.

[edit | edit source]
  • Flamer can deal damage to everyone in this server instead of an area around it.

Trivia

[edit | edit source]
  • In Journal - The Eye, it is shown that The Watcher was related to Sadan's interest in Necromancy.
  • The Watcher's eye resembles the Demon Eye from Terraria. This is further supported by the fact that both have a chance to drop item called "Optical Lens" upon their defeat.
  • The Watcher fight could be inspired by the first phase of the Brain of Cthulhu fight in Terraria, where it becomes invincible and it summons minions you must kill.
  • The Watcher will revive a player when their Wandering Soul was killed. If Wandering Soul is killed after the respective player was revived in an another way, the killing of a Wandering Soul won't have any effect.
  • The color of The Watcher's eye starts changing from a vivid green to a sickly yellow the deeper you go in the Catacombs, which slowly turns more orange when going into Master Mode.
  • The Watcher is around a decade older than Necron according to Journal - The Follower and Journal - The Apprentice, as Lathrop was born before the Calamity, while Necron was born shortly before the Wither King's attack.
  • Necron has a connection to The Watcher, calling it 'The Eye' by mentioning it in his first welcome speech.
  • It is implied that The Watcher cannot be killed.
  • One unknown undead refers to The Watcher as "Stalker" in Journal - Aftermath.
    • "Stalker" is also The Watcher's epitaph in Mort's description of the Entrance floor.
  • The Watcher's original name, Lathrop, is a reference to Dr. Emmett Lathrop Brown, more commonly known as Doc, from Back to the Future, as is his father figure, Dr. Emmett.
  • Previously, if players managed to enter the Blood Room without picking up the Blood Key, The Watcher would start spawning mobs anyway. As of May 11, 2026, known methods to achieve this without cheats have been patched, and if a player enters the Blood Room without the Blood Key being picked up first, the run is immediately failed with the following message:
    Due to violation of our server rules this instance has been terminated.
